headline: Shifting Grid Costs to Large Users
short_summary: This bill aims to shift the costs of new electrical infrastructure and capacity onto high-energy users like data centers, with the intent of reducing residential utility bills.
supporters: Governor Abigail Spanberger's administration, Democratic lawmakers, residential customers.
news_headline: Governor Pushes Data Centers to Pay More for Grid Upgrades
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger and Democratic lawmakers are urging regulators to make data centers bear more of the cost for Virginia's grid upgrades, rather than shifting these expenses to residential customers. This push comes as Dominion Energy seeks to recover $1.5 billion in transmission spending, with a significant portion tied to data center demand.

headline: Reporting Data Center Water Use
short_summary: This new law requires local water authorities to publicly report the total volume of water, including reclaimed water, provided to data centers, increasing transparency on their water consumption.
supporters: Senator Kannan Srinivasan, environmental advocates, communities concerned about water resources.
opponents: Data center industry (initially questioned being singled out).
news_headline: New Virginia Law Mandates Data Center Water Reporting
news_summary: A new Virginia law, effective January 1, 2027, requires local water authorities to publicly report the water consumption of data centers. This legislation, championed by Senator Kannan Srinivasan, aims to provide transparency regarding the industry's water usage amidst concerns about its rapid growth.

headline: Limiting Data Center Siting and Noise
short_summary: This new law requires site assessments for new high energy use facilities, including data centers, to examine sound profiles and allows localities to consider impacts on water, agriculture, and historic sites before approval.
supporters: Community residents, local governments, environmental advocates.
opponents: Data center industry (may face increased development costs and restrictions).
news_headline: Virginia Law Mandates Data Center Siting and Noise Assessments
news_summary: A new Virginia law, effective July 1, 2026, requires site assessments for new data centers to evaluate their sound profiles on nearby residential areas and schools. The legislation also grants localities the option to assess impacts on water, agriculture, and historic sites, addressing growing community concerns about data center development.
